prs.author: Epochex
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: post_writer is spawned into the task group with tg.start_soon() and the caller proceeds/yields immediately, without waiting for post_writer to actually begin consuming from write_stream. members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: post_writer is spawned into the task group with tg.start_soon() and the caller proceeds/yields immediately, without waiting for post_writer to actually begin consuming from write_stream. This creates a race where messages written by the caller before post_writer's loop starts iterating can be lost or interleaved incorrectly. Both PRs fix it the identical way: add a `task_status: TaskStatus[None] = anyio.TASK_STATUS_IGNORED` parameter to post_writer and call `task_status.started(None)` right after entering the stream context manager, which requires the caller to switch to `await tg.start(post_writer, ...)` so it actually blocks until post_writer signals readiness.

This creates a race where messages written by the caller before post_writer's loop starts iterating can be lost or interleaved incorrectly.
